thread:
incident-bot: Paging ENG-ONCALL: Alert: kv-read-fanout spike for prefix /cust/ -> backend kv-store p95 read latency 820ms, error-rate 11%. Graph: https://grafana.redwood/kv/fanout
Maria (eng-oncall): on it. seeing the same in the dashboard, errors are mostly 5xx from kv-proxy checkout.
Liam (sre): tagging in. is this localized to a region or a tenant hotset?
Maria (eng-oncall): looks skewed to us-east-1, top prefixes: /cust/alpha, /cust/gamma. heavy read amplification from a background prefetch job plus normal traffic.
Sasha (infra): initial theory: prefetch -> fanout to many keys -> eviction pressure -> kv read retries -> latency spiral. we should consider immediate mitigations: 1) global prefetch disable 2) per-tenant rate limit on reads 3) route matching prefixes to bypass cache for correctness (avoid stale reads) 4) throttle fanout at the proxy layer.
Elaine (support): any confirmed customer impact? I have two support tickets mentioning degraded embeddings generation.
Keenan (product): ok if customers see degraded results we need comms. quantify: how many tenants affected and ETA for mitigation?
Maria (eng-oncall): running quick query to enumerate tenants hitting those prefixes...
Maria (eng-oncall): (query) SELECT tenant_id, count(*) FROM proxy_logs WHERE prefix LIKE '/cust/%' AND time > now() - 5m GROUP BY tenant_id ORDER BY count DESC LIMIT 10; got 4 tenants above threshold, top two are AlphaCorp and GammaApps.
Liam (sre): recommend immediate actions in order: A) patch prefetch off B) add per-tenant read rate cap for top tenants C) add short-lived prefix bypass for correctness (read from origin for /cust/*) D) add nginx-level limit_req on proxy to cap fanout.
Sasha (infra): I'm ready to apply A and D. Maria can you handle B/C?
Maria (eng-oncall): applying A now.
Maria (eng-oncall): ```kubectl -n platform patch configmap cache-config -p '{"data":{"prefetch.enabled":"false"}}'
# verify
kubectl -n platform get configmap cache-config -o yaml | yq '.data.prefetch.enabled'
```
incident-bot: Deploy job started: cache-config-patch (ci/3456) by Maria
Maria (eng-oncall): prefetch toggled to false, config reload success, telemetry shows background prefetch queue drain starting.
Sasha (infra): applying nginx limit: ```# add to proxy rate limiting (temporary)
limit_req_zone $binary_remote_addr zone=fanout:10m rate=100r/s;
server { location / { limit_req zone=fanout burst=300 nodelay; }}
```
Sasha (infra): pushed throttle, rolling restart proxies in us-east-1.
Liam (sre): Maria, for B/C I'm giving you the internal admin API. Use caution: these are live quotas. Example command to set tenant read cap:
Maria (eng-oncall): got it. posting snippet.
Maria (eng-oncall): ```bash
curl -X POST "https://admin.internal/quotas" -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN" -d '{"tenant_id":"AlphaCorp","quota":{"read_per_sec":25}}'
```
Maria (eng-oncall): setting AlphaCorp and GammaApps read caps to 25r/s as a mitigation.
Maria (eng-oncall): applying prefix bypass for correctness for /cust/* so reads go to origin (fallback) to avoid inconsistent cached stales:
Maria (eng-oncall): ```bash
curl -X POST "https://admin.internal/cache-bypass" -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN" -d '{"prefix":"/cust/","duration_secs":900,"reason":"live mitigation - correctness"}'
```
Elaine (support): drafting a customer note to AlphaCorp and GammaApps: short note explaining degraded latencies and temporary throttling for stability. I will ask for permission to send after you confirm mitigation window.
Keenan (product): please include estimated timeline (15–30m) and that we are prioritizing correctness and will follow up with a postmortem.
Maria (eng-oncall): metrics check after changes: error-rate dropped from 11% -> 1.4% in 8 minutes, p95 latency from 820ms -> 130ms. fanout count per request reduced ~60%.
Sasha (infra): proxies stabilized, secondaries healthy. No restart loops.
Liam (sre): keeping a soft cap on the prefetched queue and watching retries. Good to hear numbers.
Maria (eng-oncall): handing off to Sasha for ongoing observation and long-lived mitigation work (Sasha, you'll take oncall? I'm going offline in 20m).
Sasha (infra): ack, taking over. I'll open a follow-up incident ticket to evaluate longer-term mitigations: smarter prefetch backoff, prefix-based cache TTLs, and adaptive fanout limits.
Elaine (support): finalizing customer note now and will send to AlphaCorp & GammaApps saying: "We applied temporary read throttling and a corrective bypass to stabilize your requests; you may see transient errors while we monitor. We're targeting to restore normal operation after health metrics remain stable for 1 hour."
Keenan (product): please schedule a postmortem with engineering and support tomorrow EOD. capture timeline, root cause, and proposal for permanent config changes.
Maria (eng-oncall): creating postmortem stub: https://confluence.redwood/incidents/2355551234 (will flesh out).
incident-bot: Incident severity reduced to P2 — mitigations applied. Notifying oncall rotation and incident leads.
Sasha (infra): monitoring window started. will report status updates every 15m. current: errors 1.2%, p95 120ms.
Maria (eng-oncall): thanks team. handing back to rotation in 18m.
Sasha (infra): note for follow-up: consider per-prefix shard limits and add a circuit-breaker in kv-proxy to avoid retry storms.
Liam (sre): agreed. will add task to roadmap.
Elaine (support): sent messages to customers. no escalations so far.
Sasha (infra): marking this thread resolved for immediate mitigations. will update incident ticket with mitigation commands and observed metrics. postmortem to include recommended changes and estimated rollout plan.
Maria (eng-oncall): thanks all. :thumbsup:
